methods.label: Scale the area and weight
methods.explanation:
Equal density and thickness mean that equal areas of the two pieces weigh the same, so their weights are proportional to their areas. Both triangles are equilateral, so their corresponding angles are equal and the triangles are similar.

The side-length scale factor is \(5/3\). Corresponding bases and heights both scale by this factor, so the area scales by its square. Therefore the second piece weighs
\[
12\left(\frac53\right)^2
=12\cdot\frac{25}{9}
=\frac{100}{3}\text{ ounces}.
\]
This is \(33\frac13\) ounces. It differs from \(33.3\) by only \(1/30\) ounce, while every other choice is more than \(13\) ounces away. The closest weight is \(33.3\) ounces, choice D.
